Wooden Puzzles for Toddlers - Educational Wooden Pattern Blocks Playset in Vehicle Transportation Shapes with Vibrant Colors, 5 Brain-Building Peg Puzzles Youngsters have special educational needs. They love to play and as parents, we want to give them things to play with that also exercise their young, curious, developing minds. A good toy for this purpose is this Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle set from Lemostaar.

Packaged in a box, this set contains 6 different dinosaur puzzles and each of the puzzles has just 6 pieces. The puzzles are each assembled on a small board measuring about 7 by 6 inches. The small size makes the puzzles just right for young kids and the bright colors are certain to get a child’s attention.

With only 6 pieces, toddlers are the age group most likely to benefit from these puzzles. Kids have a chance to show their skill as they put each of the pieces into place. Depending on a child’s interest and skill level, some may take longer than others, but most preschool age kids will be determined to assemble and show off their completed puzzle to supportive parents.

With all these pieces, there could be a tendency to lose them, but fortunately, the manufacturer includes a storage bag. You could place them back into the box, but the storage bag is better. It’s cool that the manufacturer thought to add this because it’s practical and better ensures that pieces don’t get lost.

Teaching problem- solving skills to young people can be accomplished in many ways and a toy like the Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle set from Lemostaar is useful for this purpose. With 6 puzzles and just 6 pieces each, a young person can complete each with relative ease and improve coordination and other skills in the process.

da Vinci's Room Awkward Turtle The Word Party Card Game with a Dirty Sense of Humor for Groups of 4 or More People Gave this as a gift to a recipient out of state- Due to that fact, I never felt capable of reviewing the product. Craziest thing… almost a year later, when we went On vacation and met up for dinner at the house I sent this too..(can you follow that..?!) to my happy surprise- they were all playing awkward turtles!! Yep, the game I had sent to them almost a year prior!! (could have been contrived Sure-but, from the wear and tear on the game… I knew they had been using it all along.)

Of course, we went to have Dinner with the adults at the house.. But, their group of teen/20+ yr olds were laughing hysterically in the other room having “game night“ and I promise, they were having way more fun than we were!!

I peaked in on the gameplaying and the concept looked pretty straightforward. Basically, divided into two teams… One member has an awkward word and tries to describe it to their team- if guessed correctly they get points! And the game sort of back-and-forths from there… Funny, quirky, annoying, cringe worthy, racy words all make up the options.. These kids were playing the game when we arrived- 2hr. Later we left... And they were still playing! (No! Not the same round but, plenty of rounds and all entertained long enough to still be having fun hours later.)

To me, this is the best type of endorsement one can have… Seeing a game in action and hearing the laughter as it was being played. This told me all I needed to know… The game was a hit for the crowd at hand- it kept them happily playing for hours. Combined it with the ease of which it takes to “learn” the game.. And you’ve got a winner in my book!
text_fidelity_b: da Vinci's Room Awkward Turtle The Word Party Card Game with a Dirty Sense of Humor for Groups of 4 or More People

Educational Insights Pass The Peas This game has potential, but due to its flimsy nature and low quality of organization, we didn't enjoy it as much as we could have.

The peas are just press out cardboard pieces that sit on top of cardboard pods. They are slippery and as you pass the pods, the peas slide everywhere. If you are at any size table with people sitting average distance apart, the peas will easily slip off and get messed up as you pass them.

The little bags of peas also should be color coded. Instead all of the bags are supposed to match an individual pea pod, but you have to open them up every time to look as on the outside they are all identical. At very least, they should have put in different colored strings so you could see which was what.

If they made the pods so they would lay flat instead of bending closed somewhat, and maybe have something like Velcro or magnetic surface, it would be a lot better to use. As you move around the pods it would be more secure and not so stressful.

The game has potential to be fun, but a combination of the cheap way it is made and the frustration present when trying to play, it just isn't as nice as it should be. The game is somewhat fun at first, but soon after beginning to play we just lost interest.

QTL School Stickers for Teacher Stickers for Students Laptop Kids Water Bottles Stickers Science Stickers Waterproof Back to School Stickers Packs 50Pcs I love sending Halloween cards but they don't seem complete without great stickers.

I have tried MANY kinds over the years, and THESE, are BY FAR, the BEST.

PROS:

SIZE - BIG I got exclusively for putting on envelopes, and most of them where so big, I could only put on back to seal. You may consider that a plus or minus, but they STICK out!

ADHESIVE - I noticed someone put they just have PAPER on the back and they had to glue them down. I have a feeling they just didn't realize you have to pull the paper off. The adhesion is GREAT.

PACKAGING AND PRESENTATION - Most stickers are on a sheet or a roll, these all came separately in a little packet. SO easy. I wish more stickers came this way.

QUANTITY AND QUALITY - You get a lot (I usually send out maybe 20 cards and there were 50 stickers) and I was amazed at the quality. I like the glossiness too.

VARIETY - WOW, nothing was repeated and there are ones for different age groups. Some regular Halloween type, some gross (teens and preteens would love those) and some in the middle.

ONLY CONS:

Would have been nice if a few more had been smaller or long and narrow so I could put one on the front as well.

There are some that aren't really LITTLE kid friendly.

BOTTOMLINE: WOULD DEFINITELY GET THESE AGAIN! and they were a REALLY GOOD price for what you get.

Mecha Beasts Playing Cards by Gent Supply I have a few “collectible” decks of playing cards, this one among them. These are fancy cards that are made well and I like them, but the color scheme is a bit off for the black suit cards due to the background.

I’ll start with my main complaint with these first. These are dark cards, using a dark gray background for all suits, and using a dark purple for spades and clubs. This creates a low-contrast scheme that is more difficult to see in low light, and is less than pleasant even in brighter light. This is an unfortunate choice that could have been handled better. A bright purple, or even a strange color choice like orange or blue, would have worked better.

The artwork on these is impressive. A good bit of detail went into each design and it shows. The number cards (2 -10) have small designs on them that are at times hard to see and look at without a magnifying glass, though.

This are well made cards, coated and designed so they will not stick together even in damp climates. They come in a beautiful tuck box with reflective highlights in purple.

These are not bad cards at all. They’re beautiful and they’re well made, and they have some incredible artwork. However, the color scheme is not the best and these cards would be even better if the background and black suit colors were chosen a little more thoughtfully.
text_fidelity_b: Mecha Beasts Playing Cards by Gent Supply

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 20 cars is too much at once. Nope! It is wonderful.

Days as a five year-old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 20 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 20 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels 20-Car Gift Pack."

Anthony Trendl
AmericanSpeechwriter.com
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels 20-Pack of 1:64 Scale Toy Sports & Race Cars, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary)

SGILE Remote Control Car with 2 Battery, Gift for 6-12 Years Old Kids, 1:16 15KM/H RC Drift Race Crawler Car Toy, Red [[VIDEOID:aa2775d9378faee66bb1b179a1e96566]] This car was for my son's birthday so the pressure was on as the reviews were mostly positive.

He loved it when he opened it, "that's cool!" was the exact response.
-There was no assembly necessary.
-One battery pack was in the car and needed to be connected and the spare battery was in a separate box.
-The controller did require batteries (not included).
-There was a usb charging cable for the car battery packs, but there is no wall plug (so a wall plug or usb connectable device is needed).

The battery was fully charged in the car so we got to test it right away. Good thing is that we crashed several times but no cosmetic damages (fish tank stand, kitchen table, wall (twice), coffee table, my legs (yes, both).

The car was pretty fast but not as fast as I anticipated. That is probably a good thing for my 8 year old as the crashes like meant speed was about right for his first time using this car. His birthday was a few days ago and he's played with it for several minutes each day since then with no need to charge that battery (or use the secondary battery thus far).

The battery does say it will need 3 hours to charge though so BE READY to get that second battery on the charger right when you get this car.

Overall, very satisfied. It is a 4/5 for us and would get a 5/5 if the controller came with batteries and USB charger had a wall plug.

Crayola Oil Pastels Portfolio Series, Water Soluble, Colors may vary, 12 Count (52-3612) I tried the Crayola neon pastels first and then decided to get a bigger set so I bought the portfolio crayolas set and have included a picture of all 24 colors.
They are bright with a variety of colors including black and white. Crayola has never come across as a high-end brand, but in oil pastels they are highly regarded as some of the best, and I agree. If you watch some of the videos on YouTube about how to use oil pastels you will realize how great these are. You can also see comparison videos, and the crayola brand gets very high marks. Oil pastels don't make a mess unless you use your finger to blend them, and then your finger will be a big mess. But you can clean it with baby wipes or soap and water or lotion to get down into your skin if it's dry. You can use traditional rolled paper sticks for blending also. These come packaged neatly so you can keep them in their original slots in that packaging. Besides coloring with them you can also use a wet brush to blend them, and you can layer them on top of each other or blend them together with your finger. I have also seen them covered with a clear acrylic paint and then used again on top of that paint. You can see that on YouTube. These are an inexpensive way to enjoy yourself artistically and produce beautiful results just like painting when you add the water or vodka or a blender like turpenoid.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Oil Pastels Portfolio Series, Water Soluble, Colors may vary, 12 Count (52-3612)

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll I have been around Barbie dolls my entire life. My mom collected them and my sister got into it. My daughter has had a few here and there, but none of them was the quality that this doll is. I did not expect it to be fantastic quality, but it even fell short of my lower expectations.

WHAT IS THE DOLL LIKE?
The doll comes in a clear plastic package which is not overly attractive, in fact it looks stark and not like the usual Barbie stuff. The doll itself is packaged with two pieces of plastic sticking out from inside her head. It is then attached to the board in the back so you have to cut those pieces to get it off of the backing. That means you have to be careful of the hair. Once you managed to do this, you have to stick the plastic ends back into the skull of the doll to keep the sharp ends from pricking your child or you.

The outfit is kind of cute and the colors are attractive. The doll itself is a rigid plastic doll- not the bendable twist and turn type that they have had in the past. The head piece has a knob type attachment which makes it able to move in almost any direction. The problem is in this case, the head is so easy to move it is borderline bobble head.

HOW DOES THE HAIR COLOR WORK?
The hair color looked like it would be a lot of fun! It has a plastic piece that is similar to a flat iron in shape. Inside the *flat iron* piece are a group of colored waxy blocks. The idea is that you comb the doll's hair and separate it into strands. You press the flat iron type piece over the hair, squeeze it shut as you draw the hair through and it leaves the color on the hair.

The hair is waxy in feel, probably to make the color work better than traditional Barbie hair. In this case, however, it does not seem to do much for the process. The hair colors are not too great. They come off as crumbly and waxy and very spotty on the hair. If you run your fingers over it, you will get some on your fingers. This will stain so if your child plays with this near anything white or light colored, it could stain it.

The color blocks are almost like you mix waxy crayons with silicone to make it a bit softer. The result is uneven kind of unimpressive color on the hair. It is not overly bright and does not look like the pictures promised.

THE BOTTOM LINE
My daughter was not impressed by this doll. The body is very rigid, making for a boring play toy. The hair is very uneven and has a waxy feel to it. The colors come out crumbly and uneven, and color blocks probably will only last for a day or two of constant play and then run out. The colors will stain some things so if you plan to let your child run free with this, you may regret it if you have anything white you don't want stained. The head is so easily moved that it is unpleasant to play with and use. The outfit is cute and colorful and the shoes are not too bad either.

My daughter kept saying that she expected more substantial color that was like a watercolor marker or something instead of a crumbly waxy substance that barely sticks to the hair in a few random spots. She kept taking out her other Barbie dolls and saying how much more she liked those. I give this two stars because it has a nice outfit, and if you want a disposable toy for your child, it will serve the purpose. If you want a sturdy toy they will play with over and over, I am thinking this might not be it for you.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll

VTech Kidizoom Camera - 2010 Version Kids like to do grown- up things and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera allows them to do just that. This is a fully- functioning camera specifically designed for the needs and desires of youngsters and it allows kids to take pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even upload them to a computer for further viewing and editing.

Many qualities make this camera one to consider and the first is the memory. This is sold as a child's camera, but it has a surprisingly high level of memory and is capable of holding up to 400 pictures! This is much better than I expected and with this much memory, it will take a long time before kids exceed the available space. They can walk around the house ansd snap picture after picture without worrying that the memory will fill.

Another positive aspect with the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is its durability. This camera is made from plastic with a rubberized edge that makes it easy to hold and highly resistant to breakage. My girls have dropped it several times and it continues to work regardless. It is also very entertaining. Not only can kids take their own pictures of mom, dad, the family dog, and their friends, but they can also add to the fun by using the editing feature. The silly editing allows kids a chance to take an ordinary picture and make it look funny.

So, the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is fun for kids, but are there any cons? Well, there are a few but they are minor enough to overlook. One is the viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is quite small and some images will be barely perceptible. It would be completely unacceptable to adults, but kids will likely find it perfectly fine. Then, one has to consider the picture quality. This camera has only 0.3 megapixels and that means the clarity of the pictures is well below average. Once again, kids are not likely to care. They will so enjoy having their own camera and taking their own pictures that they won't even notice or mind the fuzzy images.

Kids like to mimic adults and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is likely to be a hit with most youngsters for this and other reasons. As I said, the clarity of the photos isn't the best and the camera does have a few other minor flaws, but none of this will matter to most children. The ability to take their own pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even view them on a computer will be more than enough to please the young camerabug in your home.
text_fidelity_b: VTech Kidizoom Camera - 2010 Version

Radio Flyer Air Ride Balance Bike, Toddler Bike, Ages 1.5-5 Pink , White It is assembled easily as mine seemed to come partially assembled beyond the scope of the directions.

It looks good, has a smooth ride, with a snazzy traditional bell to alert the neighbors.That's all good, but it needs more work at the design level.

The handlebars don't seem to attach securely, but not unsafely. A 3 year-old might not be able to loosen them, but any adult certainly can. Tighten them as hard as you can.

The cover for the handlebars -- where it attaches to the headset (just above the wheel) pops off whenever the wheel is turned. It is intended to, and does, snap in when still, but should remain snapped in always.

The bike is designed, per the packaging, for 2.5-5 year-olds. My boy turns 3 in three weeks and is considered average height. He's slightly too small. Instead, the age guidelines should describe height, not age, or both. He'll grow into it so I'm not concerned.

Overall, I'll keep it, but if I were to buy a new one, I'd buy one fully assembled, maybe even used, to ensure everything was solidly connected.

TreeFortBooks.com

This pack is for the 3Doodler START -- it will NOT work with 3Doodler Create! Be sure you know which 3Doodler you have.

That said -- this is a nice addition to the 3Doodler Start collection. I've been using my 3Doodler to create embellishments for paper crafts -- primarily hand-crafted greeting cards and a little scrapbooking. The emojis and symbols in this set work well in terms of size -- perfect for my cards. I use the heart and star most often, as well as the asterisk, pound sign, and ampersand. There are two packs of filaments: blue, red, green, gray and white, mint/aqua, yellow and orange. Good colors that work with a variety of color schemes.

Overall, a good refill set with the addition of the emoji/symbol DoodleBlocks. I like it!

Brickyard Building Blocks 177 Pieces Large Building Block Toys for Children Ages 1.5-5, Bulk Block Set, Compatible with Duplo (177 pcs) We like the Lego brand, but sometimes we need a lot of bricks without paying an exorbitant amount of money. The 1,100 piece kit from Building Bricks was exactly what we were looking for. The Big Questions:
1. Do they really work well with Lego Brand Legos?
Yes - they work very well. It's difficult to tell the difference if you're not really trying hard.
2. How much cheaper are they? Is it really worth it?
It's hard to compare exact pricing here because this set does not include wheels, doors or special pieces. If I had to choose a product to compare it to, I'd probably compare it with Lego's XXL Classic Box (https://www.amazon.com/10697-Building-Large-Creator-Pieces/dp/B00XJ5C4FW). When pricing per piece, the Lego box is about 5¢ per piece. And yes, you read that right. You're dolling out a nickel for every piece of plastic with Lego's brand stamped on it. :) Building Bricks runs about 3¢ per piece. So the answer is: It's almost half the price - very worth it if you're just needing a lot of standard pieces.
As a side note: We really liked the color choices Building Bricks made. They're perfect for expanding your Lego creation palette.
text_fidelity_b: Brickyard Building Blocks 177 Pieces Large Building Block Toys for Children Ages 1.5-5, Bulk Block Set, Compatible with Duplo (177 pcs)

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Scattergories Board Game I played this when I was a kid and it's still a great game if you only have 30 minutes to spare. In 30 minutes you can easily get in 3-4 rounds of brain busting fun. This game is really about trying to mentally out maneuver your friends by coming up with words starting with whatever letter the die at the beginning of the round gave you that are unique enough to answer the prompt that no one else has thought of it. If no one else thought of your answer you get a point and so on down the prompt card each round. If your answer is the same as someone else's you both cross it out and lose that potential point.

What I love about this game is the creativity in answers and how far you can bend the rules. We always play that the group votes on whether your answer is valid or allowable since it always gets a little fuzzy as the game goes on and our competitive nature picks up. It's a mental gymnastic type of game that is face paced and frustrating but over all lots of fun and laughs with a good group. A real classic that has great replayability.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Scattergories Board Game

fansmart 39" Pull -Along Wagon for Kids with Pulling Wood Railing Panels Outdoor Wagon 10" All Terrain Air Tires 330 lbs Capacity for Beach, Garden, Sporting Events, Park（Red） I got this 'Lil Red Wagon' from Fansmart mainly for around the house use. I have a much MUCH larger garden wagon that can be pulled by hand or hooked up to your lawn and garden mower/tractor. But, it's just not convenient for doing simple things around the flower garden. This Fansmart wagon is great for that. Putting it together, I noted a few things. 1) Don't overtighten the acorn nuts. You will pop the caps right off. 2) The wood stake and slate side panels are NOT the most solidly built. The wood is soft pine and the panels are just stapled together. My advice would be to coat them very well with some clear polyurethane or other wood preservative before assembly. And, don't be too rough or careless when working with them. it's okay to put a load against them. Jut understand that there are limitations on how much abuse they can take. 3) When putting the cotter pins through the axles, to hold the wheels on, make sure you bend them all the way around the axles, to prevent any chance of a puncture or laceration from the sharp ends of the cotter pins. 4) Use your common sense in assembling the front yoke / truck assembly. The illustration is not that detailed. But, it's fairly simple. The finished front end will NOT be that tightly fitted when you're done. That's okay. It's the way it was designed. 5) The rounded pan head of all the bolts going through the pan of the wagon go ON THE INSIDE of the pan, not the outside. Even then, the heads do not seat perfectly into the holes. They do have an edge that can snag on bagged materials like mulch, potting soil, etc. My advice would be to lay a piece of cardboard or something in the bed of the wagon. The would both prevent tears in your bagged materials AND protect the finish of the wagon.

I've been using mine for hauling heavy plants around and even moving frozen goods from the deep freeze to the snow bank, during this 'winter storm of the century' that we had down here in Texas. The power was out for four days and I didn't want to lose roughly $700 in venison. Lil Red did the trick.

If anyone is old enough to remember the 'Radio Flyer' wagons that were sold a few decades ago, this wagon is kind of like that. But, not as big and not as heavily constructed. However, this wagon is good enough quality, for the price, to still earn a five star rating from me.

text_fidelity_a:
UCanaan BJD Dolls 1/4 SD Doll 18 Inch 18 Ball Jointed Doll DIY Toys with Full Set Clothes Shoes Wig Makeup, Best Gift for Girls I absolutely love dolls of all types and own hundreds of them. They range from inexpensive off-brand play dolls, legitimate BJDs, to high-end handmade artist dolls. This is likely the worst designed doll I have ever handled.

This doll has a very cute face and poses well. However, the deal-breaker is that she has No Neck! Her head sits right on her shoulders. This is very distracting because it makes it hard to look at her. I would be able to overlook so many of the other negative aspects to this doll if she had a neck like the doll in the description photos. This is very disappointing. It's such a pity as she has a very pretty face.

This is not a BJD (ball-jointed doll). This doll shares a similar aesthetic to some BJDs, but she does not have even a single ball joint. She has hinge and swivel joints only. The doll is made from at least three different types of plastic. One maybe ABS plastic, but there are no silicone components to this doll.

Her hair is pretty rooted plugs. The description led me to believe it may be a wig, but no. The plugs are evenly spaced and I do not see any bald spots. The hair fibers are soft. The eyelashes are glued strips and the eyes are inset acrylics. She has very pretty face that is painted symmetrically. The joints were very, very stiff and difficult to loosen with force. Once loosened, she does pose decently and can touch her face. She has a full outfit that is made with flawed fabric. Several threads are missing in the weave of the fabric of the skirt. The flawed fabric is very noticeable. The outfit has a shirt, vest, skirt, bloomers, knee socks and a hat. It would be a very cute outfit if the stitching was a little more straight and the fabric was not deeply flawed fabric. The material is incredibly low quality. Her shoes are light purple canvas, do not match the outfit, but are fair quality and fit her flat feet snugly.

A packet of 'accessories' are included and is confusing. They are thin plastic, various shades of pink and not to scale with the doll. The comb and 4 little hair elastics may be useful to play with the doll but otherwise they would likely not be much fun for playing with the doll and I feel would be better left out of the package. Some heeled shoes were also included in the packet and although I could put them on the doll, the straps were useless and they looked odd as she has flat feet. Little fingers would likely become frustrated trying to fasten the straps.

I looked into the UCanaan brand after ordering this doll. I was disappointed to learn that the company uses re-casted parts from legitimate BJD makers without permission. This is very sad/bad news. I would have expected better from a US retail site and find it deeply disappointing. I do not know that any pieces are made from the re-casted parts from other companies for this particular doll, but it's a serious negative point that should be noted. I cannot say with confidence this is not a re-casted doll. I would not be surprised to learn that it is.

I cannot recommend this doll. The primary reasons being she has no neck, is not as described and the company does shady business practices. This makes me very uneasy as it sets up customers for some serious disappointment. If you are looking for a budget-friendly legitimate BJD, there are other companies that make very nice lower-cost dolls. It takes a minimum amount of looking off the site to find them. If you are looking for a nice doll for display, or posing and play, please note this one has no neck and uses poor quality materials. Your money would be better spent elsewhere. I do not find this to be a good value in the least. She would be enjoyable for display if she had a neck like the doll in the description photos. I hope that this can be remedied in the future. I find this doll very disappointing and it's such a pity as she would otherwise be very cute with an alternative outfit.

I do hope you have found my honest review helpful. If you do, please click the Helpful button below. Thank you for reading my review.
text_fidelity_b: UCanaan BJD Dolls 1/4 SD Doll 18 Inch 18 Ball Jointed Doll DIY Toys with Full Set Clothes Shoes Wig Makeup, Best Gift for Girls

text_fidelity_a:
Wonder Wheels by Battat – Dump Truck, Tow Truck, Cement Truck – Toy Truck Combo Set for Toddlers Age 1 & Up (3 Pc) – 100% Recyclable , Yellow This is a mixed bag. The dump truck is GREAT! Much better than the green toys version because the dump part goes all the way vertical to dump out. YAY!!! My 5 year old was all over this, mixing all manner of unappetizing mud pies, twig sandwiches and grass clumps and moving the muck from one place to another.

The cement mixer is AWFUL. It is infuriating that they make a cement mixer with no opening to put stuff! It has this tiny little grate that lets out small amounts of dry sand or very teeny tiny pebbles. I guess you are supposed to cram it in through the tiny grate that is supposed to let stuff out? God forbid you get dirt in there and water, and it clumps up, as has happened with many other trucks in a similar vein. I had no issue turning the drum smoothly and appreciate that the drum can be angled downward to dump out, but this was pretty much the most disappointing disaster of a cement mixer I could imagine given there is no mechanism for getting stuff IN, or cleaning it. Who DOES that? That designer or committee needs to be fired.

The tow truck is mixed. I love the pull out ramp. It sticks a bit and is a little harder to use than desired, but overall good. But the hook part and the bar do not function well. The hook is stuck onto this boxy bar so it is hard to actually get it to hook to a vehicle, not impossible, but could have been done better. You can pull the bar out an inch and a half but then trying to push it back in, I injured myself/ hurt my finger. I am a grownup, so it is hard to imagine that this was truly vetted for use by toddlers if it needs that much force. Then the angling mechanism also requires a lot of oomph. My five year old can do it but finds it frustrating. 2 year old cannot.

Overall the packaging of having this set of three harmonizing full size trucks is great. Would be fun to pull out when guests come to loosen everyone up together and give everyone something to play with. But the design flaws make it hard to truly recommend. In a dry, clean sandbox, this would probably be most successful since the cement mixer would actually function.
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Wheels by Battat – Dump Truck, Tow Truck, Cement Truck – Toy Truck Combo Set for Toddlers Age 1 & Up (3 Pc) – 100% Recyclable , Yellow

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset There's a lot to love about sets like this that can be combined with other sets and used in creative ways. However, I'll say right up front that the whole point of getting this one is that you get the power booster, and the power booster, in my view, could use a big overhaul in the design.

Is it fun? Yes, without a doubt, the power booster is pretty fun. The problem? First of all, it takes 4 D batteries. Who uses D batteries nowadays? I'm lucky that we had just the right number of D battery adapters that allow us to use AA batteries instead, because otherwise I would have been in for a trip to the grocery store and I don't think it would've come cheap. What a power hog!

Second, the battery area needs to be taken apart with a screwdriver. This is fine for toys meant for the under three crowd, but for kids old enough to use a hot wheels set, it seems a little excessive and pretty irritating that every time a new set of batteries I need to become Mr. fix it and get out a screwdriver.

Third, when you actually go to play with it, the power booster is either on or off. So when the kid forgets about the hot wheels set and wanders off to go do something else, it's still sitting there using up your expensive D cell batteries. It's also noisy. I would've much preferred a button on the top that is easy for children to press that makes it work for a short period of time, such as 30 seconds. I'm guessing it is too much to ask to have a motion sensor turn it on or off or anything like that, so a limited time button that the child can find easily and press in the midst of gameplay without turning the power booster upside down would have been ideal.

That said, I think my primary criteria for evaluating hot wheels set is whether it is fun. Not fun for me, but fun for my kids. With only a little bit of help getting things set up, my three-year-old has been playing with this vigorously for two days and shows no signs of getting bored with it. We actually have a manual hot wheels ejecter to where you pull the lever back and press a button to make the car go really fast, and instead of using the power booster, we set that up for him to play with it on his own. The power booster is fun for when you make a big elaborate set up and are playing with a group of kids or with a parent for an extended period of time but to be honest I think when the batteries run down we may not replace them until there is a compelling reason to do so. It's just too noisy, and requires too much intervention from the parent to turn it on and off when it is needed and not just leave it noisily running and eating up our batteries.

The loop the loop works great with either the power booster or the manual ejection thing we already owned, and the tracks of course work with all of our other hot wheels sets.

I would probably recommend this most for people who have multiple children who will be playing with large and extended sets of hot wheels for 30 minutes or longer at a stretch. Otherwise, the power booster seems silly and kind of a waste.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Build Your Race Playset

Large Tumbling Timber Toy + Dice + Carry/Storage Bag - 54-Pc Wooden Blocks - Premium Pine Wood Floor Game for Kids & Adults - Grows from 1.5-feet to Almost 3-feet While Playing, Life Size Tower While many games make the claim that they are suitable for the whole family - this one is actually FUN for the whole family!

As most are familiar with the game Jenga, this is essentially played the same way - pull a block from the stack and place it on top. If your block causes the tower to tumble, you lose. The primary difference is the blocks are SUPERSIZED, measuring 7.1”(long) X 2.3”(wide) X 1.4”(tall). The blocks are the perfect size for little hands and kids get the hang of the game quickly and enjoy seeing the tower grow and eventually topple.

While the game’s tower begins at around 2’ it quickly grows to 4-5’+. The blocks are not only bigger but they are made of high grade pine, sanded smooth - 20 of the blocks are numbered (1-8, some numbers are duplicated while others are not) allowing players to develop a limitless number of custom games. Something we do is let the winner of each game write their name, or a short message on a block - it makes it fun to look back and remember the fun we have had during previews games.

In addition to the blocks this set comes complete with a wooden crate for storage and travel that easily doubles as a stable, flat playing surface when needed. In addition there is a white board with a dry erase marker for listing the rules you’ve set for the numbered blocks. Due to the 8 block being a one of a kind, we call it the Magic 8 Block and use that as a wild card type block - the person who pulls and places it can name whatever rule they choose.

This is a game reminiscent of games of old - no batteries, nothing electronic, it will last forever, can go anywhere to be played inside or out and is loads of fun for everyone.

This is most definitely a game set I recommend. We have loved it!

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Made to Move Doll, Orange Top Update:
I got a blue top this time to head-swap with Barbie Paleontologist. I really loved the pretty dimples of Blue Top Barbie. I hope to get another one soon. This one could even stand in flat shoes. Her ankles were just right. Some of the other Barbie Made to Move dolls had tricky little ankles with a mind all their own.
Also the peg inside their heads are slightly different, so the neck on one doll looks shorter now.
I just got Barbie Made to Move today. I read many reviews about Barbie Made to Move vs. Style Barbie. I just had to try her out. Most people who have the 2 dolls say Made to Move Barbie is a much better poser. This is very true.
I liked the rooted lashes and 2-toned hair on Style Barbie the best, so I can't say Style Barbie is a loser. Style also has the bending ankle and can wear both flats and heels. Made to move Barbie has choppy hair. I like it just the same, because my real hair is not all the same length. I thought it looked nice.
Made to Move Barbie can bend her knees all the way back and sit down on her knees. She can bend at the breast/ rib cage, but not at the waist. Style Barbie cannot do any of this.
Style Barbie can only bend her knees to sit down in a chair.
Made to Move Barbie can spread her legs out like in yoga or exercise class. Style Barbie can spread her legs very little in comparison.
Made to Move Barbie has much sturdier looking joints except in the ankles, they are almost the same. One thing I did notice was one of her ankles turns inward like she needs her electrolytes. I thought it was the shoes but I traded their shoes around and noticed the shoes were okay. I still like the natural looking poses for this doll. She is a much better choice for those who love doll dioramas and modelling clothes.

As soon as I got her out, I noticed one small dot on her foot and face both barely noticeable. To me personally, this is not a problem, but I thought I should mention it. The price was well worth it for this doll. The clothes are nice enough and stretchy so I can go ahead and pose her. I had a couple of pairs of Barbie shoes to try on her. She came barefooted. I was thrilled to find that her jointed ankle makes it possible for her to wear high heels and flat shoes made for Barbie. I have both branded and unbranded Barbie shoes that fit her. I was almost about to sell some of the shoes when I got her, but she is a keeper and loves shoes. The usual Barbie seams are kind of rough in places but that is okay, considering what I paid for her ($11.04). I consider this to be a really great buy.

text_fidelity_a:
CGE Czech Games Edition Thats A Question Excellent party game from the makers of Codenames. If you've played Codenames, then you know that is a fantastic party game, but that it requires the right group - a slow or domineering player can often mean that everyone is standing around staring at the board for an hour while they dole out perfectly configured clues. It's a fun game, but it requires the right group. That's a Question is a party game that can be played by absolutely anyone, and that, in my opinion, makes it almost a superior game.

In That's a Question!, players use cards to ask A/B style "would you rather" questions in which players attempt to guess the outcome. Based on the results, you move your pawn along the track.

The rulebook is well-written and funny, and is aware that this game is a little bit weird - attempting to give a theme to a basic Q&A style game, but it works. Of course, the game is not perfect. You are limited to only asking three different main questions, although the game does provide a wide variation of answers. There are also point modification questions which allow you to muddy up the scoring in your favor. Ultimately, the scoring was the part of the game that we found most cumbersome, and the modifiers didn't help that, simply adding a little more chaos. Scoring is also modified based on how many players are playing; as this was clearly designed as a 5-6 player game, a 4-player game has a few modifications, and the 3-player game has a fairly substantial number of scoring modifications to make it more challenging. It's nothing you can't figure out, but it is not very clean.

Overall, a good party game for 5-6. The box indicates that this is a game for ages 15+, and nothing in the content of the cards makes me think that anyone from age 7 and up can't handle.
text_fidelity_b: CGE Czech Games Edition Thats A Question

NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version I've used a LOT of drones, from professional DJI models to the cheap pocket sized tiny drones. I love flying the little ones around the house and practicing zipping in between banisters and over bookcases, and I love flying my larger DJI Phantoms and Mavic outside for real shots of landscapes and aerial photography. I was hoping this would be a good in-between product.
It is not really.
It looks a lot like the Mavic Mini, but that immediately falls apart when you hold it and realize how cheap the construction is. That's ok, it costs about 1/3 of what I paid for my Mavic Mini. But I've held cheaper drones that felt better than this. The controls are very much like the cheaper smaller drones that have been around for years (including the flip feature, which is admittedly fun), and the quality of the camera has not improved since the first cheap one I tried 5-6 years ago. Find the most basic/free cell phone you can buy from a store shelf a few years ago and the camera quality will look better than this. That was ok back then, especially since I recall paying 40-60 dollars for those drones and the cheapest DJI was closer to 800! But now, I was expecting better. At this price tag and with 2022 tech, I was hoping it would be some sort of bridge-gap product.
The downside to being larger is that it sort of doesn't fit into either category... Unlike a more expensive drone with GPS and fine tuned motors, it does not handle itself well outdoors unless there is ZERO wind (nearly impossible, especially as you climb altitude), and it is too big to fly indoors without being in danger of hitting something and actually doing damage (unlike the smaller cheaper ones). I actually can't think of a situation that I'd like to use this with: I'd recommend a smaller camera drone to play with indoors and once you are approaching the triple digit dollar amount, I'd recommend even a used Mavic Mini for outdoor flying (much more stable with GPS, and a stabilized go-pro quality camera etc).
It does come with two batteries which is nice since they go quickly, and the carrying case is pretty nice too. I guess if you're in the market for a drone like this, it DOES work so it deserves at least 3 stars, but I'm slightly disappointed with what you get for the asking price.
text_fidelity_b: NEHEME NH760 Drones with 1080P HD Camera for Adults, WIFI FPV Live Video, RC Quadcopter Foldable Drones for Kids Beginners, Headless Mode, One Key Start Toys Gifts with 2 Batteries, Upgraded Version

Radio Flyer Ultimate EZ Folding Wagon for kids and cargo, Red, Model Number: 3900 The foldable flyer is so far so good--easily put together, nicely constructed, easily foldable and relatively compact.

Packaging: It comes in a large box already folded. Separate parts are minimal: the canopy (folded), the handle, two wheels packed separately with their screws, the four rods that hold up the canopy. Everything is clearly packaged, plastic is wrapped with very easily removable tape, several soft cushions protect from banging/scratches. Took about a two minutes to pull everything out and remove them from their bags.

Assembly: You need a phillips screwdriver and a wrench. From already having the parts out of their bags and laid out to completely done and mobile took exactly 14 minutes. It’s an extremely easy, simple, and fast assembly.
1) Pull up on the handles to unfold the wagon
2) Press down on the middle panel to snap into rigidity
3) Attach the two separated wheels, each of which is labeled L or R accordingly (the label is sort of a raised letter--black on black--you may need to look closely at the wheel strut to see it. Attaching the wheels consists of dropping the wagon atop the wheel struts, placing a washer and screw, and tightening. Simple, fast, easy.
4) attach the handle--one bolt and nut. Simple, fast, easy
5) Push the four rods into the holes for the canopy and press down
6) Attach the canopy via four snaps onto the top of the rods

The holes/snaps all lined up perfectly. There was no difficulty, no manipulation, no cursing. All as easy as could be.

To fold, simply remove the canopy and lift up the center panel. Again, worked flawlessly.

It’s a mix of plastic and fabric. But the plastic doesn’t feel cheap and the fabric seem pretty rugged. Overall build quality seems solid and as if it will last through the years with little kids.

It moves smoothly and easily. It’s very light and maneuverable. The handle is not adjustable, but it does allow you to contract it for storage. There are cup holders on either side of the inside and cup holders on the outside end at the handle.

The seats have a “seat belt”. They cannot be removed, nor do they fold flat. The canopy is a nice touch for shade and rain (though it won’t stop kids getting wet if there’s any wind slanting the rain).

Really, there’s nothing at all to complain about. If you don’t mind the price, this is an excellent and convenient pick-up
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Ultimate EZ Folding Wagon for kids and cargo, Red, Model Number: 3900

It's a new skill. I'm an adult, and I got a bit on my finger the first time I tried it. I am grateful it's not the temperature of normal 3D printing filament (200-300C, and about in range of a soldering iron). With a regular pen, I'd have been in the emergency room. The skill is transferable, so once you're confident with this, you can safely move on to the real deal. They make two other models to grow into, and those take pla and abs plastic.

What I didn't like was the lack of clear instructions. There is good stuff on their website, but a better manual would have been appreciated. That's my only ding. Otherwise, this was brilliant. Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over This game is best for really young children! I'd say 2-4. My son is almost 4, but he has some learning delays, so this game has proved perfect for him. Most of the games that are sold in stores, like Wal-Mart are still too old for him. I believe in challenging him, but he just doesn't understand them yet. Again, though, this one has proved to be perfect for him. I've already ordered another game from this line, with hopes to add more along.

There's no type of competition with it. There's 6 wooden snails, a race-board, and two dice. You roll the dice and whatever color they land on, you move that colored snail up a space. If both dice land on the same color, you move that colored snail 2 spaces. Sometimes, I had to wonder what the point was! It IS a great learning tool, though. It teaches taking turns, learning colors, and counting. Plus, quality learning time with children is always a good thing.

While I received this one free for review, I honestly would have purchased it. Before I received it, I didn't even know about this line of games. My son has had fun with it, and I'm really glad that it's now part of our game collection.

Overall, I'd say if your child is very young, or has learning delays, or simply likes simple games, this is a great choice. If your child is used to more advanced games, I wouldn't bother with it. There looks to be more advanced, yet still educational games from this line that might be a better choice, though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over

text_fidelity_a:
Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone This is so awesome and it works! I thought that with how affordable it is, that it wouldn't even be able to get off the ground, but it flies great! I have to warn you that it's super hard to fly, though. This will frustrate pretty much everyone except for someone who's already an expert in quad copters. But, it's an awesome first copter to practice on. I felt that I built my skills a lot with this, and now I can fly my bigger copter a lot better than I did before I played around with this.

An awesome thing about this is that you can separately order every part of this copter. And, unlike many electronic devices, the sum of the parts is about the same as getting a new one. So, I guess you could also just get two, and when one breaks, then fix it with the other one. Or wait for them to both break and then Frankenstein a whole one back together. But, because these have such available and interchangeable parts, then I can't give it less than five stars.

The battery lasts for about five minutes of flying. Or, fifteen minutes if you're like me, and get it stuck a lot. And, the blades are all plastic, but they hurt if they run into a person. This is also really easy to get stuck on top of a roof or in a tree, so I recommend flying it in a pretty open field. They do pretty good at crash landings, too, as long as they land on grass, which was most of my landings.

It is packaged with a bunch of replacement blades, too, so you don't have to worry about breaking a few of them. They're easy to replace, too.

This listing has both the CX-10 and CX10A. The only difference is that if you depress the left stick three times on the 10A, then you go into headless mode, which is better for beginners. If you want more control, though, then you should get the CX-10. Or, you should get both, since their parts are all interchangeable.
text_fidelity_b: Cheerson CX-10 Mini 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis LED RC Quadcopter Toy Drone

Avengers Marvel Legends Iron Man Electronic Helmet - Multicolor There are a few ways to evaluate this. I'll to approach it methodically.

Appearance
Nails it. Tony Stark could wear this. While it isn't metal, they got the color and the shape so spot-on. If you are looking for a piece to display in your home or office, this is it.

Size
This will fit all but the largest heads. M.O.D.O.K and The Watcher might not fit this, but almost everyone else will.

Weight
Not too heavy, but it weighs enough to feel real. It is comfortable.

Sounds
A weak spot. They sound much like greeting card special effects.

Lights
When the lights are on, it is hard to see. Cool, but nearly blinding. That means taking this to a con might be difficult.

Taking It On/Off
It is hard to explain, but it is tricky to get right. You can, so don't worry but be aware that undoing the back is a pain in the neck.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com
text_fidelity_b: Avengers Marvel Legends Iron Man Electronic Helmet - Multicolor
